\begin{theorem}[Odd scaling cannot match a finer scale]
\lean{FABL.not_odd_scaled_eq_finer_scaled}
\label{FABL.not_odd_scaled_eq_finer_scaled}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $d,k$ be natural numbers and $z,w$ integers. If $z$ is odd and $k<d$, then $z/2^d\ne
w/2^k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree bound for resilient functions]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_booleanFunctionF₂Encoding_le_of_isResilient}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.IsResilient, FABL.algebraicDegree_le_iff, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.booleanFunctionF₂Encoding, FABL.booleanRealEmbedding, FABL.exists_odd_restrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree, FABL.isLowDegreeFourierRegular_zero_iff_forall_mean_signRestriction_eq, FABL.mean, FABL.not_odd_scaled_eq_finer_scaled, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff_encoding_empty, FABL.signRestriction, FABL.zeroFixedSign}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p150-b004}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $k$ be a natural number. If $f$ is $k$-resilient and
$k<n-1$, then the algebraic degree of its encoding as a function on the Boolean cube
over the two-element field is at most $n-k-1$.
\end{theorem}
